Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital Course:
The patient initially presented with acute myocardial infarction and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention with stent implantation. However, residual stenoses and stent malappositions were observed, and the patient was referred for CABG. Echocardiogram revealed a left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 19%, and enhanced computed tomography showed bilateral occlusions of the internal thoracic arteries and a small fragile sternum after sternoturnover fixation. Left thoracotomy was performed without cardiopulmonary bypass, and the saphenous vein and radial artery grafts were successfully anastomosed to the target vessels. The patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged on postoperative day 12.

Hospital Course Summary:
A 53-year-old man presented with acute myocardial infarction and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention with stent implantation. Residual stenoses and stent malappositions were observed, and the decision was made to perform CABG due to the left anterior descending artery, high lateral branch, and left circumflex artery lesions. The patient had a left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 19%, a bilateral internal thoracic artery occlusion, and a small fragile sternum after sternoturnover fixation, which made the left thoracotomy approach the preferred method. The procedure was performed successfully without cardiopulmonary bypass, and the patient had an uneventful recovery, resulting in a patent bypass graft of all target vessels. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 12 without any issues.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this episode is the acute myocardial infarction, with residual multivessel coronary stenoses treated by off-pump CABG. The MI falls within four weeks of onset, so it is still coded as acute even though the CABG came after the PCI. This places it in chapter I, category I21.

CODE: I21
